title: Grateful Dead Live at The Eureka Municipal Auditorium on 1968-01-20

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard captures a blistering early‑68 set with a smoking Clementine, Spanish Jam and New Potato > Born Cross Eyed sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a surprisingly clear vintage sound‑board capture that lets every instrument shine – from Jerry’s soaring Garcia solo in the Spanish Jam to the tight organ work of Pigpen. Musically the show is a fire‑storm of rare material: an inspired Clementine, the jazzy New Potato/Caboose segue into Born Cross Eyed and a punchy Spanish Jam that many reviewers call “the best of ’68”. Energy is off the charts and the transitions feel seamless, making this one of the most coveted early‑68 performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Over thirty detailed reviews overwhelmingly praise both the performance (rare songs, high energy) and the soundboard quality (crisp, clear). The show is described as exceptional with only minor complaints about short jams, yielding a near‑perfect combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clear for a 1968 tape; minimal analog hiss, good instrument separation. Vocals are low in the mix but not detrimental. No major drop‑outs reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare songs flow together tightly – Clementine leads straight into New Potato, which segues into Born Cross Eyed and then a smoldering Spanish Jam that drops into a brief Caution before the pre‑Dark Star riff. Transitions are praised as smooth and natural.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solo tone is described as “glowing tubes”, “bassy leads” and “astonishing” especially in Spanish Jam and Clementine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass work gets kudos for “bassy leads at the start of Caution” and overall solid foundation throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen (organ) is highlighted as being “at his best”, with some debate over whether it’s Pigpen or Tom Constanten, but the keyboard texture is praised highly.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart are called “the finest” of the era; their drumming is noted as a driving force behind the show’s fire.
